results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database (VFB). VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three main parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the mushroom body, including images, neuron information, parts, subclasses, and lineage clones. For example, VFB has annotated [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body. The user can explore these data further by querying VFB for specific information, such as images of the mushroom body or neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The LPLC2 visual neuron type is a type of visual neuron with specific characteristics and functions. According to VFB, the cell body of LPLC2 lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. It has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, allowing it to detect looming stimuli. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. The arbors of LPLC2 span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. LPLC2 projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. Its activity elicits a jump escape response. VFB records show that there are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and they are cholinergic. VFB does not currently hold detailed connectivity data for LPLC2 beyond its projection to the PVLP.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, with a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle, as described by Thomas and Wyman (1984). There is one of these cells per hemisphere, according to Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), and Sturner et al. (2025). The giant fiber neuron can be identified by its large descending axon, which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective, as noted by Power (1948) and Koto et al. (1981).

VFB holds various data related to the giant fiber neuron, including [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01. The downstream connectivity classes for DNp01 are represented by [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records, while the upstream connectivity classes for DNp01 are represented by [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records.

The giant fiber neuron is also associated with specific genetic tools and expression patterns, with VFB returning 10 genetic tool/expression pattern rows for the giant fiber neuron. It is considered a primary neuron, as mentioned in publications by Allen et al. (1998), Dorkenwald et al. (2024), and Schlegel et al. (2024).

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), Power (1948), Allen et al. (1998), Dorkenwald et al. (2024), and Schlegel et al. (2024), among others. 

To further explore the giant fiber neuron, you can examine the available images, splits, and transgene expression records, as well as the downstream and upstream connectivity classes.
